content.title: About
content.content: The Whopper is Burger King's signature burger, first introduced in 1957. It features a 100‑gram flame‑grilled beef patty, topped with lettuce, tomato, pickles, onions, mayonnaise, ketchup and mustard, all sandwiched in a soft sesame‑seed bun.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Whopper was the first "big" burger that Burger King marketed as larger and more filling than competitors'.
In the 1990s the brand used the slogan "Have it your way" to highlight the Whopper's customisation options.
In 2020 Burger King released a limited‑edition Japanese Whopper with a rice bun.
In 2021 the chain introduced a plant‑based Whopper using an Impossible Foods patty.
The Whopper often appears in marketing stunts where its size is compared to everyday objects, such as a soccer ball.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat is a good source of heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The patty supplies B12, B6 and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Lettuce, tomato and pickles add dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: A modest amount of monounsaturated fats from the beef and sauces can support heart health when consumed in moderation.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: A single Whopper contains about 660 kcal, which can contribute to weight gain if eaten frequently.

items.title: Saturated fat and cholesterol
items.content: The beef patty and sauces are rich in saturated fats, which may raise cholesterol levels when consumed in excess.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Sauces and the bun can be high in salt, which is a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The bun contains gluten, and the sauces may include dairy or egg, triggering allergic reactions.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Some sauce formulations may contain small amounts of trans fats, which should be limited.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The Whopper is served in a split bun, allowing you to add or remove toppings to suit your taste. It can be eaten by hand or cut into sections for easier handling. In many markets extra toppings such as bacon or cheese are offered.

content.title: Storage
content.content: A freshly prepared Whopper should be eaten immediately. If you need to store it, wrap tightly in foil and keep refrigerated for up to 24 hours. Reheat in an oven or grill to retain bun crispness.
